title: Model specification
description:
WHAT WAS FITTED, as data -- a mechanism, an architecture, a library of candidate terms. A first-class, versioned, content-addressed artifact, for exactly the reasons a calibration is one: it is revised independently of the data, many results depend on it, and revising it must be able to tell you which of them went stale.

This is deliberately NOT a name in a capability registry. A registry is right for a method vocabulary -- `laplace`, `hold_constant`, `d-optimal` -- which is small, stable, and shared. Mechanisms are none of those things: they are combinatorially many, they are generated automatically by mechanism discovery and reduction, and comparing competing ones IS the science. A registry entry per candidate would mean a pull request per hypothesis, which makes the central activity of this project the most expensive thing in it.

Content addressing gives what the registry was protecting: two specifications that differ anywhere hash differently, so they cannot collide on one id, and no coordination is needed to guarantee it. Switching mechanism is then `--in <other spec id>`, and the provenance chain records which one produced which fit.

Distinct from `model`: that is a FITTED model, a research product carrying trained parameters, training data, and metrics. This is the hypothesis before any of that exists. A fitted `model` cites the spec it was fitted from.

spec_id.description: Identifier for this specification. Content-addressed in practice: change any part of the specification and this becomes a different id, because a fit against a silently edited mechanism is a fit nobody can reproduce.

family.description: Which model class this specifies. Selects the body required below. This IS a controlled vocabulary -- families are few, stable, and shared -- which is the distinction between what belongs in a registry and what belongs in an artifact.

name.description: Human-facing label. NOT an identifier: two specifications may legitimately share a name while differing, which is precisely why the id is a content hash and not this.

description.description: What this specification is for, and what distinguishes it from its near neighbours. The field that makes a list of twelve candidate mechanisms readable.

derived_from.description: The specification this one was produced from -- by reduction, by adding a step, by a discovery run. Makes a family of candidates a graph rather than a pile.

derivation.description: How it was derived from that parent, in one line. 'removed step 3 and refitted', 'DRC-reduced at 500 K', 'proposed by discover_mechanism run 14'.
examples: reduced by degree of rate control

parameter_transform.description: The space free parameters are fitted in. Rate constants span decades, so log10 is usual; an implementation that fits in a different space from the one declared here produces uncertainty intervals that mean something else.

provenance.description: Present when the specification was generated by a tool -- a discovery or reduction run -- rather than authored by hand.

mechanism.description: Required when family is microkinetic. A declarative reaction network: sites, gas species, adsorbates, and elementary steps.

composition.description: Element counts, so a mass balance is checkable rather than assumed.

steps.description: Elementary steps, in a fixed order. The order is part of the specification because free parameters are packed in it, so reordering the steps changes what a fitted parameter vector means.

equation.description: The step, written with '+' and a single arrow. Reversibility is declared separately rather than encoded in the arrow, so that turning one step irreversible is a one-field edit and shows up as a one-field diff.

reversible.description: Whether the reverse rate constant is a free parameter. THE field that distinguishes competing variants of one mechanism, which is why it is required rather than defaulted -- an unstated reversibility is the difference between an eight-parameter and a ten-parameter fit.

constraint.description: A constraint that fixes this step's reverse constant instead of fitting it -- typically thermodynamic closure from an overall equilibrium constant. Recorded because it changes the number of free parameters and therefore what every uncertainty interval means.

kind.description: thermodynamic_closure: reverse constant derived from the others plus an overall equilibrium constant. fixed: held at `value`. equilibrated: step assumed at quasi-equilibrium.

source.description: Where the constraint's numbers come from -- e.g. 'NIST Shomate polynomials for CO, O2, CO2'. A closure whose thermochemistry is unstated cannot be reproduced.

activity_basis.description: What gas activities in the rate expressions are. Sets the units of every adsorption rate constant, and mixing this up between a fit and its reuse is a silent factor of 10^5.

gas_constant_J_per_mol_K.description: Declared so the energy unit of any reported activation energy is fixed. Pass 8.617e-5 to work in eV.

architecture.description: Required when family is neural_ode or rnn. Enough to rebuild the model: layer sizes, activations, and anything else that changes what is fitted.

seed.description: Initialisation seed. Required in spirit for anything with random initialisation: an unrecorded seed makes a trained network unreproducible in exactly the way an unrecorded LFSR seed makes a waveform unreproducible.

library.description: Required when family is sparse_regression. The candidate term library and the sparsity rule -- the two things that decide what such a method can discover, and the two most often left in code.

free_parameters.description: The free parameters in the order an implementation packs them, with bounds. Declared here rather than in code so two implementations of one specification produce comparable parameter vectors -- otherwise 'k4' means position 7 in one fit and position 3 in another, and every comparison is silently wrong.

bounds.description: Lower and upper, in the declared parameter_transform's space.

reaction_system.description: The reaction this specification is a model of. Free text in 0.2.0, matching the dataset field of the same name so a specification and the data it is fitted to can be filtered together.

references.description: Where this mechanism comes from -- DOIs, or a citation of the paper that proposed it. A mechanism with no stated origin is one nobody can argue with.

notes.description: Anything a reader needs that the structured fields do not carry: known limitations, the conditions it was proposed for, what it is NOT expected to reproduce.

thermodynamics.description: OPTIONAL, and it changes what the free parameters ARE. When present with parameterisation 'arrhenius-detailed-balance', the specification's free parameters are physical: (log10A, Ea) per step and (dH_ads, dS_ads) per adsorbate; every reverse rate constant follows from detailed balance against the named gas-phase thermochemistry, and a conforming fit treats all provided runs JOINTLY across temperature. This block lives in the SPECIFICATION because the parameterisation is a property of the hypothesis, not of the fitting code -- switching between per-temperature and thermodynamically-consistent treatments is a different spec id, not a different tool. DRAFT (2026-08): real-data-revision branch, for the September meeting.

parameterisation.description: Which coordinates the FORWARD constants are fitted in; reverse constants follow detailed balance either way. 'arrhenius-detailed-balance' fits (log10A, Ea) per step. 'tst-detailed-balance' ANCHORS the prefactor at its transition-state value -- kT/h for a surface step, the collision-limited impingement rate for a step whose forward side consumes a gas molecule -- and fits (dS#, dH#) instead, so dS# = 0 is textbook transition-state theory and a sign constraint on dS# is a physical statement rather than a numerical guardrail. Per-temperature fitting is the ABSENCE of this block, not an enum value -- a spec without it keeps today's meaning unchanged.

gas_parents.description: Per adsorbate: the gas species (with stoichiometry) its formation enthalpy and entropy are measured RELATIVE to, e.g. {'CO*': {'CO': 1}, 'O*': {'O2': 0.5}}. The parent choice defines what dH_ads MEANS, so it is specification content; implementations must check it balances the adsorbate's declared composition.

gas_data_source.description: The tag of the vendored gas-phase thermochemistry the closure computes from, e.g. 'gas-thermo-codata-shomate-2026-08-25'. Hashed into every fit through this document's artifact id; an implementation whose vendored data does not match must refuse.

pressure_Pa.description: Reactor pressure for the mole-fraction/standard-state correction. Default 101325.

notes.description: Anything else a reader needs about the thermodynamic treatment.

site_area_m2.description: Area per active site, m^2. Required in spirit by 'tst-detailed-balance' and meaningless without it: the collision anchor is an impingement flux per unit AREA, while a manifest reports site density per unit MASS, and converting between them needs a specific surface area that transient records do not carry. So this is the one declared assumption behind the adsorption anchor, and it is specification content because the value used is part of what the fitted activation entropies MEAN. ~1e-19 m^2 (10 A^2) is the conventional single-site area. NOTE that an active-site FRACTION is deliberately not a parameter anywhere: it would enter as -R ln f, perfectly correlated with dS#, so only the combination is estimable and fitting both would be structurally non-identifiable.

reactor.description: OPTIONAL, and it changes what the MODEL PREDICTS. Its absence is the gradientless treatment -- the catalyst sees one gas composition, there is no axial coordinate, and the observable is a per-site rate times a fitted scale -- which is what a spec without this block has always meant, unchanged. When present with kind 'axially-dispersed-packed-bed', the gas becomes a STATE with a spatial coordinate, the model predicts outlet mole fractions rather than a scaled rate, and the site-count scale factor stops being a free parameter because the bed supplies it. This block lives in the SPECIFICATION and not in a capability registry for two reasons. A rate constant fitted under one reactor model is not the same quantity as one fitted under another, so the reactor is part of what the hypothesis asserts and has to be hashed with it. And a registry entry is a bare name: it could not carry the node count or the discretisation, and a hashed name beside unhashed numbers is the failure mode CONTRACT.md section 2 calls the worst one available. Bed GEOMETRY is deliberately NOT here -- that is measured, belongs to the experiment, and rides on the protocol's `bed` block. DRAFT (2026-08): axial-PDE branch, for the September meeting.

kind.description: The only implemented value. The gradientless treatment is the ABSENCE of this block, not an enum value, so no existing specification changes meaning.

nodes.description: Axial nodes, inlet included. Hashed: it is a discretisation choice that moves the answer. The reference implementation uses 101; on the B29 bed the outlet is converged by about 21 with a second-order upwind scheme, and the binding constraint is the timestep rather than the grid.

convection.description: Convective stencil. 'upwind2' is the reference implementation's. 'upwind1' adds numerical dispersion of u*dz/2, which competes with the physical coefficient on a coarse grid -- available so that can be measured rather than argued.

outlet.description: Outlet closure. Both hold dC/dz = 0 in the dispersion term. 'psu' additionally drops the convective term in the last cell, reproducing the reference exactly -- that cell then has no outflow, so it is not conservative, though a uniform field still satisfies it and both closures share a steady state. 'convective' keeps the outflow.

rate_basis.description: What one unit of reaction rate means, and therefore the units of every rate constant. 'per-catalyst-mass' (the default, and the reference implementation's): rates in mol/(kg s), coverages evolving as r/Ct. 'per-site': rates as turnover frequencies (1/s), coverages evolving as r directly, with the bed's measured site density entering only the gas-coupling factor -- which makes the constants unit-identical to the gradientless treatment's and directly comparable across the two reactors. Hashed through the specification body like everything else here; two specs differing only in rate basis are different hypotheses about what the numbers mean.

velocity.description: Whether the superficial velocity responds to the injector pulse. Opening the injector raises the total molar flow and dilutes the carrier, so 'frozen' does not merely blur the oxygen response, it removes most of it. Hashed because it changes the prediction, not the cost.

dispersion.description: Tag for the correlation set the axial dispersion coefficient is computed from: tortuosity-corrected molecular diffusion plus a mechanical term at particle Peclet 2, with Fuller binary diffusivities combined by Wilke's rule. Named rather than numeric because it is computed, not fitted -- and an implementation whose correlations differ must refuse rather than compute something else under this document's id.

inlet_reconstruction.description: How the unlogged inlet is recovered. Part of the hypothesis: the inlet is an input to every fitted constant, so two reconstructions are not comparable fits.

method.description: 'tracer-shift' recovers the inlet from a co-fed inert tracer displaced by one empty-bed residence time -- exact for plug flow, approximate in a dispersing bed, and what the reference does. 'declared' uses a logged valve schedule, which is what section 1.4 asks the reactor to start recording and would retire this whole block.

tracer.description: The inert species co-fed with the pulsed stream, e.g. 'Ar'. A tracer in the CARRIER measures nothing about the switching.

notes.description: Anything else a reader needs about the reactor treatment.

maturity.description: How much weight someone else may put on this record. Absent means `sandbox`, which is true of everything written before the field existed.

stewards.description: Who is answerable for THIS record, replacing the spoke's list rather than merging with it. Absent means the spoke's stewards apply, which is the usual case.
